title: Apply Operations to Make Sum of Array Greater Than or Equal to k
summary: Given a positive integer k, start with an array containing a single element 1.
statement: Given a positive integer k, start with an array containing a single element 1. You can either increment an element by 1 or duplicate an element. Determine the least number of operations needed to ensure the sum of the array elements is at least k.
constraints: k is a positive integer; begin with the one-element array [1].
One operation either increments one array value by one or appends a duplicate of an existing value.
Return the minimum operations required to make the array sum at least k.
reference_solution:
def minimum_array_sum_operations(k):
    answer=k-1
    for increments in range(k):
        value=increments+1
        duplicates=(k+value-1)//value-1
        answer=min(answer,increments+duplicates)
    return answer

hints: After increments create a maximum value x, every duplication should copy x because no smaller copy improves the sum.
Enumerate the number of increments a, then compute how many total copies of value a+1 are needed.
For a=0..k-1, operations=a+ceil(k/(a+1))-1; take the minimum.
Any operation sequence has a largest built value and number of elements, requiring at least x-1 increments and elements-1 duplications; enumeration realizes every such bound.
